fields.label: Layer height
fields.upstreamHelp: Slicing height for each layer. Smaller layer height means more accurate and more printing time

fields.label: Initial layer height
fields.upstreamHelp: Height of initial layer. Making initial layer height thick slightly can improve build plate adhension

fields.label: Mixed color sublayer
fields.upstreamHelp: Enable mixed color sublayer splitting. When enabled, layers containing mixed color filaments will be split into sub-layers to achieve color mixing effects.

fields.label: Default
fields.upstreamHelp: Default line width if some line width is set to be zero

fields.label: Initial layer
fields.upstreamHelp: Line width of initial layer

fields.label: Outer wall
fields.upstreamHelp: Line width of outer wall

fields.label: Inner wall
fields.upstreamHelp: Line width of inner wall

fields.label: Top surface
fields.upstreamHelp: Line width for top surfaces

fields.label: Sparse infill
fields.upstreamHelp: Line width of internal sparse infill

fields.label: Internal solid infill
fields.upstreamHelp: Line width of internal solid infill

fields.label: Support
fields.upstreamHelp: Line width of support

fields.label: Seam position
fields.upstreamHelp: The start position to print each part of outer wall

fields.label: Seam placement away from overhangs(experimental)
fields.upstreamHelp: Ensure seam placement away from overhangs for alignment and backing modes.

fields.label: Seam gap
fields.upstreamHelp:
In order to reduce the visibility of the seam in a closed loop extrusion, the loop is interrupted and shortened by a specified amount.
This amount as a percentage of the current extruder diameter. The default value for this parameter is 15

fields.label: Smart scarf seam application
fields.upstreamHelp: Apply scarf joints only to smooth perimeters where traditional seams do not conceal the seams at sharp corners effectively.

fields.label: Scarf application angle threshold
fields.upstreamHelp:
This option sets the threshold angle for applying a conditional scarf joint seam.
If the seam angle within the perimeter loop exceeds this value (indicating the absence of sharp corners), a scarf joint seam will be used. The default value is 155°.

fields.label: Scarf around entire wall
fields.upstreamHelp: The scarf extends to the entire length of the wall.

fields.label: Scarf steps
fields.upstreamHelp: Minimum number of segments of each scarf.

fields.label: Scarf joint for inner walls
fields.upstreamHelp: Use scarf joint for inner walls as well.

fields.label: Override filament scarf seam setting
fields.upstreamHelp: Overrider filament scarf seam setting and could control settings by modifier.

fields.label: Scarf seam type
fields.upstreamHelp: Set scarf seam type for this filament. This setting could minimize seam visibiliy.

fields.label: Scarf start height
fields.upstreamHelp: This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the current layer height.

fields.label: Scarf slope gap
fields.upstreamHelp: In order to reduce the visiblity of the seam in closed loop, the inner wall and outer wall are shortened by a specified amount.

fields.label: Scarf length
fields.upstreamHelp: Length of the scarf. Setting this parameter to zero effectively disables the scarf.

fields.label: Wipe speed
fields.upstreamHelp: The wipe speed is determined by the speed setting specified in this configuration.If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 80%), it will be calculated based on the travel speed setting above.The default value for this parameter is 80%

fields.label: Role-based wipe speed
fields.upstreamHelp: The wipe speed is determined by speed of current extrusion role. e.g if a wipe action is executed immediately following an outer wall extrusion, the speed of the outer wall extrusion will be utilized for the wipe action.

fields.label: Slice gap closing radius
fields.upstreamHelp: Cracks smaller than 2x gap closing radius are being filled during the triangle mesh slicing. The gap closing operation may reduce the final print resolution, therefore it is advisable to keep the value reasonably low.

fields.label: Resolution
fields.upstreamHelp: G-code path is generated after simplifying the contour of model to avoid too many points and gcode lines in the gcode file. Smaller value means higher resolution and more time to slice

fields.label: Arc fitting
fields.upstreamHelp: Enable this to get a G-code file which has G2 and G3 moves. And the fitting tolerance is the same as resolution

fields.label: X-Y hole compensation
fields.upstreamHelp: Holes of object will be grown or shrunk in XY plane by the configured value. Positive value makes holes bigger. Negative value makes holes smaller. This function is used to adjust size slightly when the object has assembling issue

fields.label: X-Y contour compensation
fields.upstreamHelp: Contour of object will be grown or shrunk in XY plane by the configured value. Positive value makes contour bigger. Negative value makes contour smaller. This function is used to adjust size slightly when the object has assembling issue

fields.label: Auto circle contour-hole compensation
fields.upstreamHelp: Expirment feature to compensate the circle holes and circle contour. This feature is used to improve the accuracy of the circle holes and contour within the diameter below 50mm. Only support PLA Basic, PLA CF, PET CF, PETG CF and PETG HF.

fields.label: User Customized Offset
fields.upstreamHelp: If you want to have tighter or looser assemble, you can set this value. When it is positive, it indicates tightening, otherwise, it indicates loosening

fields.label: Elephant foot compensation
fields.upstreamHelp: Shrink the initial layer on build plate to compensate for elephant foot effect

fields.label: Precise wall
fields.upstreamHelp: Improve shell precision by adjusting outer wall spacing. This also improves layer consistency.

fields.label: Precise Z height
fields.upstreamHelp: Enable this to get precise z height of object after slicing. It will get the precise object height by fine-tuning the layer heights of the last few layers. Note that this is an experimental parameter.

fields.label: Ironing Type
fields.upstreamHelp: Ironing is using small flow to print on same height of surface again to make flat surface more smooth. This setting controls which layer being ironed

fields.label: Ironing speed
fields.upstreamHelp: Print speed of ironing lines

fields.label: Ironing flow
fields.upstreamHelp: The amount of material to extrude during ironing. Relative to flow of normal layer height. Too high value results in overextrusion on the surface

fields.label: Ironing line spacing
fields.upstreamHelp: The distance between the lines of ironing

fields.label: Ironing inset
fields.upstreamHelp: The distance to keep the from the edges of ironing line. 0 means not apply.

fields.label: ironing direction
fields.upstreamHelp: Angle for ironing, which controls the relative angle between the top surface and ironing

fields.label: Wall generator
fields.upstreamHelp: Classic wall generator produces walls with constant extrusion width and for very thin areas is used gap-fill. Arachne engine produces walls with variable extrusion width

fields.label: Wall transitioning threshold angle
fields.upstreamHelp: When to create transitions between even and odd numbers of walls. A wedge shape with an angle greater than this setting will not have transitions and no walls will be printed in the center to fill the remaining space. Reducing this setting reduces the number and length of these center walls, but may leave gaps or overextrude

fields.label: Wall transitioning filter margin
fields.upstreamHelp: Prevent transitioning back and forth between one extra wall and one less. This margin extends the range of extrusion widths which follow to [Minimum wall width - margin, 2 * Minimum wall width + margin]. Increasing this margin reduces the number of transitions, which reduces the number of extrusion starts/stops and travel time. However, large extrusion width variation can lead to under- or overextrusion problems. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter

fields.label: Wall transition length
fields.upstreamHelp: When transitioning between different numbers of walls as the part becomes thinner, a certain amount of space is allotted to split or join the wall segments. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter

fields.label: Wall distribution count
fields.upstreamHelp: The number of walls, counted from the center, over which the variation needs to be spread. Lower values mean that the outer walls don't change in width

fields.label: Minimum wall width
fields.upstreamHelp: Width of the wall that will replace thin features (according to the Minimum feature size) of the model. If the Minimum wall width is thinner than the thickness of the feature, the wall will become as thick as the feature itself. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter

fields.label: Minimum feature size
fields.upstreamHelp: Minimum thickness of thin features. Model features that are thinner than this value will not be printed, while features thicker than the Minimum feature size will be widened to the Minimum wall width. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter

fields.label: Order of walls
fields.upstreamHelp: Print sequence of inner wall and outer wall.

fields.label: Print infill first
fields.upstreamHelp: Order of wall/infill. false means print wall first.

fields.label: Bridge flow
fields.upstreamHelp: Decrease this value slightly(for example 0.9) to reduce the amount of material for bridge, to improve sag

fields.label: Thick bridges
fields.upstreamHelp: If enabled, bridges are more reliable, can bridge longer distances, but may look worse. If disabled, bridges look better but are reliable just for shorter bridged distances.

fields.label: Bridge counterbore holes
fields.upstreamHelp:
This option creates bridges for counterbore holes, allowing them to be printed without support. Available modes include:
1. None: No bridge is created
2. Partially Bridged: Only a part of the unsupported area will be bridged
3. Sacrificial Layer: A full sacrificial bridge layer is created

fields.label: Object flow ratio
fields.upstreamHelp: The flow ratio set by object, the meaning is the same as flow ratio.

fields.label: Top surface flow ratio
fields.upstreamHelp: This factor affects the amount of material for top solid infill. You can decrease it slightly to have smooth surface finish

fields.label: Initial layer flow ratio
fields.upstreamHelp: This factor affects the amount of material for the initial layer

fields.label: Only one wall on top surfaces
fields.upstreamHelp: Use only one wall on flat top surface, to give more space to the top infill pattern. Could be applied on topmost surface or all top surface.

fields.label: Top area threshold
fields.upstreamHelp: The min width of top areas in percentage of perimeter line width.

fields.label: Only one wall on first layer
fields.upstreamHelp: Use only one wall on the first layer of model

fields.label: Detect overhang wall
fields.upstreamHelp: Detect the overhang percentage relative to line width and use different speed to print. For 100 percent overhang, bridge speed is used.

fields.label: Smooth speed discontinuity area
fields.upstreamHelp: Add the speed transition between discontinuity area.

fields.label: Smooth coefficient
fields.upstreamHelp: The smaller the number, the longer the speed transition path. 0 means not apply.

fields.label: Avoid crossing wall
fields.upstreamHelp: Detour and avoid traveling across wall which may cause blob on surface (when travel length greater than Travel distance threshold)

fields.label: Avoid crossing wall - Max detour length
fields.upstreamHelp: Maximum detour distance for avoiding crossing wall. Don't detour if the detour distance is larger than this value. Detour length could be specified either as an absolute value or as percentage (for example 50%) of a direct travel path. Zero to disable

fields.label: Avoid crossing wall - Includes support
fields.upstreamHelp: Including support while avoiding crossing wall.

fields.label: Smoothing wall speed along Z(experimental)
fields.upstreamHelp: Smoothing outwall speed in z direction to get better surface quality. Print time will increases. This does not work on spiral vase mode.

fields.label: Wall loops
fields.upstreamHelp: Number of walls of every layer

fields.label: Alternate extra wall
fields.upstreamHelp: Add an extra wall on alternating layers to improve layer bonding and part strength without the full cost of a permanent extra wall.

fields.label: Embedding the wall into the infill
fields.upstreamHelp: Embedding the wall into parts where the wall loops are absent ensures that the wall connects seamlessly to the infill.

fields.label: Detect thin wall
fields.upstreamHelp: Detect thin wall which can't contain two line width. And use single line to print. Maybe printed not very well, because it's not closed loop

fields.label: Interface shells
fields.upstreamHelp: Force the generation of solid shells between adjacent materials/volumes. Useful for multi-extruder prints with translucent materials or manual soluble support material

fields.label: Top surface pattern
fields.upstreamHelp: Line pattern of top surface infill

fields.label: Top surface density
fields.upstreamHelp: Density of top surface infill, 100% means a fully solid filled top layer.Lower values create a textured top surface, at 0%, only the walls are created on the top layer.Intended for aesthetic or functional purposes, not to fix issues such as over-extrusion.

fields.label: Top solid layers
fields.upstreamHelp: This is the number of solid layers of top shell, including the top surface layer. When the thickness calculated by this value is thinner than top shell thickness, the top shell layers will be increased

fields.label: Top shell thickness
fields.upstreamHelp: The number of top solid layers is increased when slicing if the thickness calculated by top shell layers is thinner than this value. This can avoid having too thin shell when layer height is small. 0 means that this setting is disabled and thickness of top shell is absolutely determained by top shell layers

fields.label: Top paint penetration layers
fields.upstreamHelp: This is  the number of layers of top paint penetration.

fields.label: Bottom surface pattern
fields.upstreamHelp: Line pattern of bottom surface infill, not bridge infill

fields.label: Bottom surface density
fields.upstreamHelp: Density of bottom surface infill, 100% means a fully solid filled top layer.Lower values create a textured bottom surface, Intended for aesthetic or functional purposes, not to fix issues such as over-extrusion.WARNING: Lowering this value may negatively affect bed adhesion.

fields.label: Bottom shell layers
fields.upstreamHelp: This is the number of solid layers of bottom shell, including the bottom surface layer. When the thickness calculated by this value is thinner than bottom shell thickness, the bottom shell layers will be increased

fields.label: Bottom shell thickness
fields.upstreamHelp: The number of bottom solid layers is increased when slicing if the thickness calculated by bottom shells layers is thinner than this value. This can avoid having too thin shell when layer height is small. 0 means that this setting is disabled and thickness of bottom shell is absolutely determained by bottom shell layers

fields.label: Bottom paint penetration layers
fields.upstreamHelp: This is the number of layers of bottom paint penetration.

fields.label: Use infill instead of top and bottom surfaces
fields.upstreamHelp: Using infill instead of top and bottom surfaces.

fields.label: Internal solid infill pattern
fields.upstreamHelp: Line pattern of internal solid infill. if the detect narrow internal solid infill be enabled, the concentric pattern will be used for the small area.

fields.label: Sparse infill density
fields.upstreamHelp: Density of internal sparse infill, 100% means solid throughout

fields.label: Fill multiline
fields.upstreamHelp: Using multiple lines for the infill pattern, if supported by infill pattern.

fields.label: Sparse infill pattern
fields.upstreamHelp: Line pattern for internal sparse infill

fields.label: Skin infill pattern
fields.upstreamHelp: Line pattern for skin

fields.label: Skin infill density
fields.upstreamHelp: The portion of the model's outer surface within a certain depth range is called the skin. This parameter is used to adjust the density of this section.When two regions have the same sparse infill settings but different skin densities, This area will not be split into two separate regions.default is as same as infill density.

fields.label: Skeleton infill pattern
fields.upstreamHelp: Line pattern for skeleton

fields.label: Skeleton infill density
fields.upstreamHelp: The remaining part of the model contour after removing a certain depth from the surface is called the skeleton. This parameter is used to adjust the density of this section.When two regions have the same sparse infill settings but different skeleton densities, their skeleton areas will develop overlapping sections.default is as same as infill density.

fields.label: Infill lock depth
fields.upstreamHelp: The parameter sets the overlapping depth between the interior and skin.

fields.label: Skin infill depth
fields.upstreamHelp: The parameter sets the depth of skin.

fields.label: Skin line width
fields.upstreamHelp: Adjust the line width of the selected skin paths.

fields.label: Skeleton line width
fields.upstreamHelp: Adjust the line width of the selected skeleton paths.

fields.label: Symmetric infill y axis
fields.upstreamHelp: If the model has two parts that are symmetric about the y-axis, and you want these parts to have symmetric textures, please click this option on one of the parts.

fields.label: Infill shift step
fields.upstreamHelp: This parameter adds a slight displacement to each layer of infill to create a cross texture.

fields.label: Lattice angle 1
fields.upstreamHelp: The angle of the first set of 2D lattice elements in the Z direction. Zero is vertical.

fields.label: Lattice angle 2
fields.upstreamHelp: The angle of the second set of 2D lattice elements in the Z direction. Zero is vertical.

fields.label: Infill rotate step
fields.upstreamHelp: This parameter adds a slight rotation to each layer of infill to create a cross texture.

fields.label: Length of sparse infill anchor
fields.upstreamHelp: Connect a sparse infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over sparse infill line width. Slicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than infill_anchor_max is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to this parameter, but no longer than anchor_length_max. Set this parameter to zero to disable anchoring perimeters connected to a single infill line.

fields.label: Maximum length of sparse infill anchor
fields.upstreamHelp: Connect a sparse infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over sparse infill line width. Slicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than this parameter is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to infill_anchor, but no longer than this parameter. Set this parameter to zero to disable anchoring.

fields.label: Filter out tiny gaps
fields.upstreamHelp: Filter out gaps smaller than the threshold specified. Gaps smaller than this threshold will be ignored

fields.label: Infill/Wall overlap
fields.upstreamHelp: Infill area is enlarged slightly to overlap with wall for better bonding. The percentage value is relative to line width of sparse infill

fields.label: Monotonic line travel extend
fields.upstreamHelp: Enable this option to extend the travel distance between lines, improving the adhesion between the monotonic line infill and the walls.(percent to line width)

fields.label: Infill direction
fields.upstreamHelp: Angle for sparse infill pattern, which controls the start or main direction of line

fields.label: Bridge direction
fields.upstreamHelp: Bridging angle override. If left to zero, the bridging angle will be calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided angle will be used for external bridges. Use 180°for zero angle.

fields.label: Minimum sparse infill threshold
fields.upstreamHelp: Sparse infill area which is smaller than threshold value is replaced by internal solid infill

fields.label: Infill combination
fields.upstreamHelp: Automatically Combine sparse infill of several layers to print together to reduce time. Wall is still printed with original layer height.

fields.label: Detect narrow internal solid infill
fields.upstreamHelp: This option will auto detect narrow internal solid infill area. If enabled, concentric pattern will be used for the area to speed printing up. Otherwise, rectilinear pattern is used defaultly.

fields.label: Ensure vertical shell thickness
fields.upstreamHelp: Add solid infill near sloping surfaces to guarantee the vertical shell thickness (top+bottom solid layers)

fields.label: Detect floating vertical shells
fields.upstreamHelp: Detect overhang paths in vertical shells and slow them by bridge speed.

fields.label: Initial layer
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed of initial layer except the solid infill part

fields.label: Initial layer infill
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed of solid infill part of initial layer

fields.label: Outer wall
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed of outer wall which is outermost and visible. It's used to be slower than inner wall speed to get better quality.

fields.label: Inner wall
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed of inner wall

fields.label: Small perimeters
fields.upstreamHelp: This setting will affect the speed of perimeters having radius <= small perimeter threshold(usually holes). If expressed as percentage (for example: 80%) it will be calculated onthe outer wall speed setting above. Set to zero for auto.

fields.label: Small perimeter threshold
fields.upstreamHelp: This sets the threshold for small perimeter length. Default threshold is 0mm

fields.label: Sparse infill
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed of internal sparse infill

fields.label: Internal solid infill
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed of internal solid infill, not the top and bottom surface

fields.label: Vertical shell speed
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed for vertical shells with overhang regions. If expressed as percentage (for example: 80%) it will be calculated onthe internal solid infill speed above

fields.label: Top surface
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed of top surface infill which is solid

fields.label: Slow down for overhang
fields.upstreamHelp: Enable this option to slow printing down for different overhang degree
Speed for line of wall which has degree of overhang between 10% and 25% line width. 0 means using original wall speed
Speed for line of wall which has degree of overhang between 25% and 50% line width. 0 means using original wall speed
Speed for line of wall which has degree of overhang between 50% and 75% line width. 0 means using original wall speed
Speed for line of wall which has degree of overhang between 75% and 100% line width. 0 means using original wall speed
Speed of 100%% overhang wall which has 0 overlap with the lower layer.

fields.label: Slow down by height
fields.upstreamHelp: Enable this option to slow printing down by height

fields.label: Starting height
fields.upstreamHelp: The height starts to slow down

fields.label: Ending height
fields.upstreamHelp: The height finishes slowing down, Ending height should be larger than Starting height, or the slowing down will not work!

fields.label: Bridge
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed of bridge and completely overhang wall

fields.label: Gap infill
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed of gap infill. Gap usually has irregular line width and should be printed more slowly

fields.label: Support
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed of support

fields.label: Support interface
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed of support interface

fields.label: Travel
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed of travel which is faster and without extrusion

fields.label: Normal printing
fields.upstreamHelp: The default acceleration of both normal printing and travel except initial layer

fields.label: Travel
fields.upstreamHelp: The acceleration of travel except initial layer

fields.label: Short travel
fields.upstreamHelp:
Acceleration used for short travel moves near external perimeters. Short travels are moves shorter than the 'Retraction minimum travel' distance.

Lower values (e.g., 250-500 mm/s²) reduce ringing artifacts on sharp corners without significantly impacting print time.

Set to 0 to disable (uses normal travel acceleration).

fields.label: Initial layer travel
fields.upstreamHelp: The acceleration of travel of initial layer

fields.label: Initial layer
fields.upstreamHelp: Acceleration of initial layer. Using a lower value can improve build plate adhensive

fields.label: Outer wall
fields.upstreamHelp: Acceleration of outer wall. Using a lower value can improve quality

fields.label: Inner wall
fields.upstreamHelp: Acceleration of inner walls. 0 means using normal printing acceleration

fields.label: Top surface
fields.upstreamHelp: Acceleration of top surface infill. Using a lower value may improve top surface quality

fields.label: Sparse infill
fields.upstreamHelp: Acceleration of sparse infill. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 100%), it will be calculated based on the default acceleration.

fields.label: Enable accel_to_decel
fields.upstreamHelp: Klipper's max_accel_to_decel will be adjusted automatically

fields.label: accel_to_decel
fields.upstreamHelp: Klipper's max_accel_to_decel will be adjusted to this percent of acceleration

fields.label: Default
fields.upstreamHelp: Default jerk

fields.label: Outer wall
fields.upstreamHelp: Jerk of outer walls

fields.label: Inner wall
fields.upstreamHelp: Jerk of inner walls

fields.label: Infill
fields.upstreamHelp: Jerk of infill

fields.label: Top surface
fields.upstreamHelp: Jerk of top surface

fields.label: First layer
fields.upstreamHelp: Jerk of first layer

fields.label: Travel
fields.upstreamHelp: Jerk of travel

fields.label: Max volumetric slope positive
fields.upstreamHelp: This experimental setting is used to limit the speed of change in extrusion rate. A value of 1.8 mm³/s² ensures, that a change from the extrusion rate of 1.8 mm³/s (0.45mm extrusion width, 0.2mm extrusion height, feedrate 20 mm/s) to 5.4 mm³/s (feedrate 60 mm/s) will take at least 2 seconds.

fields.label: Max volumetric slope negative
fields.upstreamHelp: This experimental setting is used to limit the speed of change in extrusion rate. A value of 1.8 mm³/s² ensures, that a change from the extrusion rate of 1.8 mm³/s (0.45mm extrusion width, 0.2mm extrusion height, feedrate 20 mm/s) to 5.4 mm³/s (feedrate 60 mm/s) will take at least 2 seconds.

fields.label: Enable support
fields.upstreamHelp: Enable support generation.

fields.label: Type
fields.upstreamHelp: normal(auto) and tree(auto) is used to generate support automatically. If normal(manual) or tree(manual) is selected, only support enforcers are generated

fields.label: Style
fields.upstreamHelp:
Style and shape of the support. For normal support, projecting the supports into a regular grid will create more stable supports (default), while snug support towers will save material and reduce object scarring.
For tree support, slim style will merge branches more aggressively and save a lot of material, strong style will make larger and stronger support structure and use more materials, while hybrid style is the combination of slim tree and normal support with normal nodes under large flat overhangs. Organic style will produce more organic shaped tree structure and less interfaces which makes it easer to be removed. The default style is organic tree for most cases, and hybrid tree if adaptive layer height or soluble interface is enabled.

fields.label: Threshold angle
fields.upstreamHelp: Support will be generated for overhangs whose slope angle is below the threshold.

fields.label: On build plate only
fields.upstreamHelp: Don't create support on model surface, only on build plate

fields.label: Support critical regions only
fields.upstreamHelp: Only create support for critical regions including sharp tail, cantilever, etc.

fields.label: Remove small overhangs
fields.upstreamHelp: Remove small overhangs that possibly need no supports.

fields.label: Raft layers
fields.upstreamHelp: Object will be raised by this number of support layers. Use this function to avoid warping when print ABS

fields.label: Raft contact Z distance
fields.upstreamHelp: Z gap between object and raft. Ignored for soluble interface

fields.label: Support/raft base
fields.upstreamHelp: Filament to print support base and raft. "Default" means no specific filament for support and current filament is used

fields.label: Support/raft interface
fields.upstreamHelp: Filament to print support interface. "Default" means no specific filament for support interface and current filament is used

fields.label: Avoid interface filament for base
fields.upstreamHelp: Avoid using support interface filament to print support base if possible.

fields.label: Enable ironing support interface
fields.upstreamHelp: Ironing is using small flow to print on same height of surface again to make flat surface more smooth. This setting controls whether support interface or raft interface will be ironned.Support ironing could only works on solid interface,that is, support_interface_spacing was zero and support_interface_pattern was't grid

fields.label: Support ironing speed
fields.upstreamHelp: Print speed of ironing lines

fields.label: Support ironing flow
fields.upstreamHelp: The amount of material to extrude during ironing. Relative to flow of normal layer height. Too high value results in overextrusion on the surface

fields.label: Support ironing line spacing
fields.upstreamHelp: The distance between the lines of ironing

fields.label: Support ironing inset
fields.upstreamHelp: The distance to keep the from the edges of ironing line. 0 means not apply.

fields.label: Support ironing direction
fields.upstreamHelp: Angle for ironing, which controls the relative angle between the top surface and ironing

fields.label: Initial layer density
fields.upstreamHelp: Density of the first raft or support layer

fields.label: Initial layer expansion
fields.upstreamHelp: Expand the first raft or support layer to improve bed plate adhesion, -1 means auto

fields.label: Support wall loops
fields.upstreamHelp: This setting specifies the count of support walls in the range of [-1,2]. -1 means auto, and 0 means allowing infill-only mode where support is thick enough.

fields.label: Top Z distance
fields.upstreamHelp: The z gap between the top support interface and object

fields.label: Bottom Z distance
fields.upstreamHelp: The z gap between the bottom support interface and object

fields.label: Base pattern
fields.upstreamHelp: Line pattern of support

fields.label: Base pattern spacing
fields.upstreamHelp: Spacing between support lines

fields.label: Pattern angle
fields.upstreamHelp: Use this setting to rotate the support pattern on the horizontal plane.

fields.label: Top interface layers
fields.upstreamHelp: Number of top interface layers

fields.label: Bottom interface layers
fields.upstreamHelp: Number of bottom interface layers

fields.label: Interface pattern
fields.upstreamHelp: Line pattern of support interface. Default pattern for support interface is Rectilinear Interlaced

fields.label: Top interface spacing
fields.upstreamHelp: Spacing of interface lines. Zero means solid interface.And zero spacing is required to access the enable_support_ironing option

fields.label: Bottom interface spacing
fields.upstreamHelp: Spacing of bottom interface lines. Zero means solid interface

fields.label: Normal Support expansion
fields.upstreamHelp: Expand (+) or shrink (-) the horizontal span of normal support

fields.label: Support/object xy distance
fields.upstreamHelp: XY separation between an object and its support

fields.label: Z overrides X/Y
fields.upstreamHelp: When top z distance overrides support/object xy distance, give priority to ensuring that supports are generated beneath overhangs, and a gap of the same size as top z distance is leaved with the model. Whereas in the opposite case, the gap between supports and the model follows support/object xy distance all the time. Only recommended to enable when using HybridTree.

fields.label: Support/object first layer gap
fields.upstreamHelp: XY separation between an object and its support at the first layer.

fields.label: Don't support bridges
fields.upstreamHelp: Don't support the whole bridge area which makes support very large. Bridge usually can be printing directly without support if not very long

fields.label: Max bridge length
fields.upstreamHelp: Max length of bridges that don't need support. Set it to 0 if you want all bridges to be supported, and set it to a very large value if you don't want any bridges to be supported.

fields.label: Independent support layer height
fields.upstreamHelp: Support layer uses layer height independent with object layer. This is to support customizing z-gap and save print time.This option will be invalid when the prime tower is enabled.

fields.label: Branch distance
fields.upstreamHelp: This setting determines the distance between neighboring tree support nodes.

fields.label: Branch diameter
fields.upstreamHelp: This setting determines the initial diameter of support nodes.

fields.label: Branch angle
fields.upstreamHelp: This setting determines the maximum overhang angle that t he branches of tree support allowed to make.If the angle is increased, the branches can be printed more horizontally, allowing them to reach farther.

fields.label: Branch diameter angle
fields.upstreamHelp: The angle of the branches' diameter as they gradually become thicker towards the bottom. An angle of 0 will cause the branches to have uniform thickness over their length. A bit of an angle can increase stability of the tree support.

fields.label: Skirt loops
fields.upstreamHelp: Number of loops for the skirt. Zero means disabling skirt

fields.label: Skirt height
fields.upstreamHelp: How many layers of skirt. Usually only one layer

fields.label: Skirt distance
fields.upstreamHelp: Distance from skirt to brim or object

fields.label: Brim type
fields.upstreamHelp: This controls the generation of the brim at outer and/or inner side of models. Auto means the brim width is analysed and calculated automatically.

fields.label: Brim width
fields.upstreamHelp: Distance from model to the outermost brim line

fields.label: Brim-object gap
fields.upstreamHelp: A gap between innermost brim line and object can make brim be removed more easily

fields.label: Enable
fields.upstreamHelp: The wiping tower can be used to clean up the residue on the nozzle and stabilize the chamber pressure inside the nozzle, in order to avoid appearance defects when printing objects.

fields.label: Skip points
fields.upstreamHelp: The wall of prime tower will skip the start points of wipe path

fields.label: Internal ribs
fields.upstreamHelp: Enable internal ribs to increase the stability of the prime tower.

fields.label: Width
fields.upstreamHelp: Width of prime tower

fields.label: Max speed
fields.upstreamHelp: The maximum printing speed on the prime tower excluding ramming.

fields.label: Brim width
fields.upstreamHelp: Brim width of prime tower, negative number means auto calculated width based on the height of prime tower.

fields.label: Infill gap
fields.upstreamHelp: Infill gap

fields.label: Rib wall
fields.upstreamHelp: The wall of prime tower will add four ribs and make its cross-section as close to a square as possible, so the width will be fixed.

fields.label: Extra rib length
fields.upstreamHelp: Positive values can increase the size of the rib wall, while negative values can reduce the size.However, the size of the rib wall can not be smaller than that determined by the cleaning volume.

fields.label: Rib width
fields.upstreamHelp: Rib width is always less than half the prime tower side length.

fields.label: Fillet wall
fields.upstreamHelp: The wall of prime tower will fillet

fields.label: Enable tower interface features
fields.upstreamHelp: When enabled, use dedicated temperature, pre-extrusion and purge settings for prime tower interface layers (where different materials meet), to improve multi-material tool change quality.

fields.label: No sparse layers (experimental)
fields.upstreamHelp: If enabled, the wipe tower will not be printed on layers with no toolchanges. On layers with a toolchange, extruder will travel downward to print the wipe tower. User is responsible for ensuring there is no collision with the print.

fields.label: Flush into objects' infill
fields.upstreamHelp: Purging after filament change will be done inside objects' infills. This may lower the amount of waste and decrease the print time. If the walls are printed with transparent filament, the mixed color infill will be seen outside. It will not take effect, unless the prime tower is enabled.

fields.label: Flush into this object
fields.upstreamHelp: This object will be used to purge the nozzle after a filament change to save filament and decrease the print time. Colours of the objects will be mixed as a result. It will not take effect, unless the prime tower is enabled.

fields.label: Flush into objects' support
fields.upstreamHelp: Purging after filament change will be done inside objects' support. This may lower the amount of waste and decrease the print time. It will not take effect, unless the prime tower is enabled.

fields.label: Slicing Mode
fields.upstreamHelp: Use "Even-odd" for 3DLabPrint airplane models. Use "Close holes" to close all holes in the model.

fields.label: Print sequence
fields.upstreamHelp: Print sequence, layer by layer or object by object

fields.label: Spiral vase
fields.upstreamHelp: Spiralize smooths out the z moves of the outer contour. And turns a solid model into a single walled print with solid bottom layers. The final generated model has no seam

fields.label: Smooth Spiral
fields.upstreamHelp: Smooth Spiral smoothes out X and Y moves as wellresulting in no visible seam at all, even in the XY directions on walls that are not vertical

fields.label: Max XY Smoothing
fields.upstreamHelp: Maximum distance to move points in XY to try to achieve a smooth spiralIf expressed as a %, it will be computed over nozzle diameter

fields.label: Timelapse
fields.upstreamHelp: If smooth or traditional mode is selected, a timelapse video will be generated for each print. After each layer is printed, a snapshot is taken with the chamber camera. All of these snapshots are composed into a timelapse video when printing completes. If smooth mode is selected, the toolhead will move to the excess chute after each layer is printed and then take a snapshot. Since the melt filament may leak from the nozzle during the process of taking a snapshot, prime tower is required for smooth mode to wipe nozzle.

fields.label: Fuzzy Skin
fields.upstreamHelp: Randomly jitter while printing the wall, so that the surface has a rough look. This setting controls the fuzzy position

fields.label: Fuzzy skin generator mode
fields.upstreamHelp:
Displacement: Pattern is formed by shifting the nozzle sideways from the original path.
Extrusion: Pattern is formed by varying the amount of extruded plastic (nozzle path stays straight).
Combined: Displacement + Extrusion. Similar look to Displacement but fills gaps between perimeters.
Note: Extrusion and Combined only work when fuzzy skin thickness is not greater than the printed line width.

fields.label: Fuzzy skin noise type
fields.upstreamHelp:
Noise type to use for fuzzy skin generation:
Classic: Classic uniform random noise.
Perlin: Perlin noise, which gives a more consistent texture.
Billow: Similar to perlin noise, but clumpier.
Ridged Multifractal: Ridged noise with sharp, jagged features. Creates marble-like textures.
Voronoi: Divides the surface into voronoi cells, and displaces each one by a random amount. Creates a patchwork texture.

fields.label: Fuzzy skin point distance
fields.upstreamHelp: The average distance between the random points introduced on each line segment

fields.label: Fuzzy skin thickness
fields.upstreamHelp: The width within which to jitter. It's adversed to be below outer wall line width

fields.label: Fuzzy skin feature size
fields.upstreamHelp: The base size of the coherent noise features, in mm. Higher values will result in larger features.

fields.label: Fuzzy skin noise octaves
fields.upstreamHelp: The number of octaves of coherent noise to use. Higher values increase the detail of the noise, but also increase computation time.

fields.label: Fuzzy skin noise persistence
fields.upstreamHelp: The decay rate for higher octaves of the coherent noise. Lower values will result in smoother noise.

fields.label: Apply fuzzy skin to first layer
fields.upstreamHelp: Whether to apply fuzzy skin on the first layer.

fields.label: Enable clumping detection
fields.upstreamHelp: Enable clumping detection

fields.label: Order-independent overlap carving
fields.upstreamHelp: When enabled, overlapping model parts are carved by bounding-box size so smaller embedded parts are not removed by larger parts due to volume order.

fields.label: Use beam interlocking
fields.upstreamHelp: Generate interlocking beam structure at the locations where different filaments touch. This improves the adhesion between filaments, especially models printed in different materials.

fields.label: Interlocking depth of a segmented region
fields.upstreamHelp: Interlocking depth of a segmented region. It will be ignored if "mmu_segmented_region_max_width" is zero or if "mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth"is bigger then "mmu_segmented_region_max_width". Zero disables this feature.

fields.label: Interlocking beam width
fields.upstreamHelp: The width of the interlocking structure beams.

fields.label: Interlocking direction
fields.upstreamHelp: Orientation of interlock beams.

fields.label: Interlocking beam layers
fields.upstreamHelp: The height of the beams of the interlocking structure, measured in number of layers. Less layers is stronger, but more prone to defects.

fields.label: Interlocking depth
fields.upstreamHelp: The distance from the boundary between filaments to generate interlocking structure, measured in cells. Too few cells will result in poor adhesion.

fields.label: Interlocking boundary avoidance
fields.upstreamHelp: The distance from the outside of a model where interlocking structures will not be generated, measured in cells.

fields.label: Sparse infill filament
fields.upstreamHelp: Filament to print internal sparse infill.

fields.label: Solid infill
fields.upstreamHelp: Filament to print solid infill

fields.label: Walls
fields.upstreamHelp: Filament to print walls

fields.label: Reduce infill retraction
fields.upstreamHelp: Controls whether retraction is skipped when traveling within the infill area. "Auto" enables this optimization for filaments with low metal stickiness (e.g. PLA) and disables it for medium/high metal stickiness filaments (e.g. PETG) to avoid oozing artifacts. "Enabled" always skips retraction in infill areas regardless of filament type. "Disabled" always retracts normally.

fields.label: Add line number
fields.upstreamHelp: Enable this to add line number(Nx) at the beginning of each G-Code line

fields.label: Exclude objects
fields.upstreamHelp: Enable this option to add EXCLUDE OBJECT command in g-code for klipper firmware printer

fields.label: Filename format
fields.upstreamHelp: User can self-define the project file name when export

fields.label: Post-processing Scripts
fields.upstreamHelp: If you want to process the output G-code through custom scripts, just list their absolute paths here. Separate multiple scripts with a semicolon. Scripts will be passed the absolute path to the G-code file as the first argument, and variables of settings also can be read

fields.label: Process notes
fields.upstreamHelp: You can put your notes regarding the process here.
